course_description:
A survey of influential theories, concepts, and ideas that inform the historical and contemporary practice of planning. Economic concepts, social and behavioural theory, and systems of governance and administration will be examined and related to planning theory and practice. Students will select and explore one influential idea in-depth to creatively and cogently relate this topic to planning practice.

This course introduces the foundational theories and concepts that inform planning strategy and practice. Effective planners need a broad understanding of key areas including economics and markets, government and politics, health, innovation and technology, community development and social infrastructure, climate change, housing, design and heritage, and social justice.

The course exposes students to a range of concepts, challenges, and ideas that shape the planning and design of regions, cities, and communities. It also develops the research and communication skills needed for success in Years 2–4 of the planning program. Reflecting the current housing crisis in Australia and globally, housing serves as a central theme through which students examine the interaction between planning policy and these broader foundational issues.

course_contacts.notes: Student consultations are welcomed and encouraged. Please email the Course Coordinator to make a time.

course_aims: The aim of this course is to introduce students to the range of issues that influence planning including economics and markets, government, governance, health, education, housing, climate change, crime/safety and design. While some of these issues will be considered in more depth in other BRTP courses, many of the other issues will only be considered in this course.

learning_outcomes.description: Describe and apply theories of planning to real-world situations.
Understand the role of government and governance in Australia at the federal, state and local levels.
Understand how and why economics influences urban and regional planning.
Understand and explain the range of social and cultural issues and challenges that face the planning profession.
Understand and explain how the housing, health and community sectors interface with the planning profession.
Understand and explain how climate change affects planning now and into the future.
Understand the importance of design and heritage in planning

assessment_details.title: Assessment 3: Presentation
assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Assessment Rationale Students will prepare a compelling presentation on a foundational theory, idea, or concept in urban policy, planning or housing. Students will base their presentation upon the results of their annotated bibliography (Assessment 2). In this scenario, you are preparing a presentation for a civic leader (e.g. Lord Mayor or Minister for Planning). The presentation must be engaging, succinct and communicate key findings from your research. The civic leader needs to be convinced of the relevance of the issue to the spatial and urban planning strategy, and why they should consider implementing your findings in their city or region. Presentations will be in Weeks 11-13 during scheduled lecture and practical times. Students are required to attend the scheduled session and answer questions about their research and analysis and should be prepared to answer questions on the day. Alternative presentation mode (e.g., an online presentation) must be discussed with and approved by the course coordinator. A presentation schedule will be posted on Blackboard. Note: Assessment 2 and Assessment 3 are linked. In-person assessment prohibits use of AI or MT: This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description
